verses.text: In Tiberius Caesar’s fifteenth year as emperor—while Pontius Pilate governed Judea, Herod ruled Galilee, his brother Philip ruled Ituraea and Trachonitis, and Lysanias ruled Abilene—
during the high priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas, God’s message came to Zacharias’s son John out in the wilderness.
John traveled all around the Jordan, preaching a baptism that showed people were turning back to God so their sins could be forgiven. 🌊
This is what Isaiah the prophet wrote: “A voice is calling out in the wilderness: ‘Get the Lord’s road ready; make his paths straight.”
“‘Every valley will be filled, every mountain and hill brought low. Crooked roads will become straight, and rough roads smooth.”
“‘Then everyone will see God’s salvation.’”
John told the crowds coming out to be baptized, “You bunch of snakes! Who warned you to run from the coming judgment?”
“Live in a way that shows you’ve truly turned back to God. And don’t start saying, ‘Abraham is our father.’ I’m telling you, God can raise up children for Abraham from these stones!”
“Even now the axe is already at the trees’ roots. Every tree that doesn’t produce good fruit gets cut down and thrown into the fire.” 🔥
The crowds asked him, “So what should we do?”
He answered, “If you have two coats, share one with someone who has none. If you have food, do the same.”
Tax collectors came to be baptized too. They asked him, “Teacher, what should we do?”
He told them, “Don’t collect more than the amount you’re authorized to take.”
Some soldiers asked, “What about us? What should we do?” He said, “Don’t shake anyone down or accuse anyone falsely. Be satisfied with your pay.”
The people were full of expectation. Everyone was wondering privately whether John might be the Christ.
John answered them all, “I baptize you with water, but someone stronger than me is coming. I’m not worthy to loosen his sandal strap. He’ll baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.”
“His winnowing fork is in his hand. He’ll clear out his threshing floor, gather the wheat into his barn, and burn the chaff with fire that can’t be put out.”
John used many other strong appeals to encourage the people and share the good news with them.
But John also called out Herod the ruler for marrying Herodias, his brother’s wife, and for all the evil things he had done.
Herod added one more evil to the list: he locked John up in prison.
When all the people had been baptized, Jesus was baptized too. As he was praying, heaven opened,
and the Holy Spirit came down on him in a bodily form, like a dove. A voice came from heaven: “You are my beloved Son. I’m pleased with you.” 🕊️
Jesus was about thirty when he began his work. People assumed he was Joseph’s son; Joseph was Heli’s son.
Heli’s line ran through Matthat, Levi, Melchi, Jannai, and Joseph.
Then came Mattathias, Amos, Nahum, Esli, and Naggai.
Then Maath, Mattathias, Semein, Joseph, and Judah.
Then Joanan, Rhesa, Zerubbabel, Shealtiel, and Neri.
Then Melchi, Addi, Cosam, Elmodam, and Er.
Then Jose, Eliezer, Jorim, Matthat, and Levi.
Then Simeon, Judah, Joseph, Jonan, and Eliakim.
Then Melea, Menan, Mattatha, Nathan, and David.
Then Jesse, Obed, Boaz, Salmon, and Nahshon.
Then Amminadab, Aram, Hezron, Perez, and Judah.
Then Jacob, Isaac, Abraham, Terah, and Nahor.
Then Serug, Reu, Peleg, Eber, and Shelah.
Then Cainan, Arphaxad, Shem, Noah, and Lamech.
Then Methuselah, Enoch, Jared, Mahalaleel, and Cainan.
Then Enos, Seth, Adam—and ultimately God.
